beats.vo: Getting your steps on Koshiqa is simple. It takes less than two minutes. Just one time setup.
beats.was: Koshiqa reads your steps from Google Fit. Two minutes, start to finish.
beats.why: Less flashy, more warm. Added the one-time framing.

beats.vo: Just open Koshiqa and tap “Start My Steps.”
beats.was: Koshiqa's ready when you are — tap Start My Steps.
beats.why: Dropped “when you are ready” — do-it-now framing.
flags: UI copy — Screen CTA should change too — “Find/Count my Steps”.

beats.vo: Here's what Google Fit will ask you for. Four quick things that you should know.
beats.was: Here's what Fit will ask you for. Worth a read — it's four quick things.
beats.why: Full product name; dropped “Worth a read”.

beats.vo: First, Koshiqa will take you to the Play Store. Download Google Fit and open it.
beats.was: Koshiqa takes you straight to the Play Store. Install it.
beats.why: “Install” is a heavier word — dropped from the line and the card.
flags: UI copy — Remove “Install” from the screen CTA too.

beats.vo: If you already have Google Fit, it becomes a lot easier and you can directly jump to row #15
beats.was: Then open it. Already have Fit? You'll see Open right away.
beats.why: Turned the branch into a skip-ahead.
flags: Open question — “row #15” is a spreadsheet reference, not something that can be said aloud. It needs to become a step number — and which one is ambiguous: row 15 of the sheet is step 14 (choose the account in Koshiqa), which skips past step 12 (“Connect Google fit”) and step 13 (the permission).

beats.vo: Just like every app, it needs an account. Google Fit would need an email id to save your steps.
beats.was: Fit wants an account to work with.

beats.vo: Choose the account you want to use for your steps - and remember this account. You’ll need to select the same account when you come back to Koshiqa in the end.
beats.was: Pick the one you want your steps under, and keep it in mind — Koshiqa asks for it again at the end.

beats.vo: A quick intro, then the part that matters.
Gender, birthday, weight, height. Google Fit uses these to turn your movement into real distance and calories.
beats.was: Gender, birthday, weight, height. Fit uses these to turn your movement into real distance and calories.
beats.why: Kept, with the full product name.

beats.vo: Next, turn on Activity Tracking. This is important - it allows Google Fit to count your steps while you carry your phone with you. If this is not on, Google Fit won't be able to count your steps during your walk or runs.
beats.was: Turn on activity tracking — this is what counts your steps while your phone's in your pocket.
beats.why: Added the negative side at the same time.

beats.vo: Allow the permission, and you're done with Google Fit.
beats.was: Allow it, and it starts counting.

beats.why: Cut — the completion signal moved into the previous line.

beats.vo: Now come back to Koshiqa and tap “Connect Google Fit.”
beats.was: Head back to Koshiqa and tap Connect Google fit.
beats.why: Sequence marker; label quoted as it appears.

beats.vo: Same permission, this time for Koshiqa. Allow it.
beats.was: Same permission, this time for Koshiqa.
beats.why: Every beat ends on the action.

beats.vo: And remember — choose the same Google account you selected in Google Fit. This gets your data from Google Fit to Koshiqa. If the email Id doesn't match, your Google Fit will show steps but Koshiqa won't.
beats.was: Choose the account you used in Fit. That's what links the two.
beats.why: Callback, mechanism, and the symptom the viewer would actually see.

beats.vo: Your steps will now start coming into Koshiqa. And if you ever want to check or change the connected account, you can see it right here and in your account settings.
beats.was: Your steps start coming through — and your account's shown right there if you ever want to switch it.

beats.vo: Now just keep your phone with you. Koshiqa will take care of the rest.
beats.was: From here it runs on its own.
beats.why: Ends on an action the viewer owns.
